description: Cuts an incoming phasor into steps and disrupts them at random, one step at a time

params.text: How many steps the phasor cycle is cut into, 1 to 64, at 1 by default
Scales the STEPS CV before it is added to the knob, -1 to +1; at full depth 5V spans the whole 64-step range
How often a step gets disrupted: none at all fully counter-clockwise, every step fully clockwise
Scales the CHANCE CV before it is added to the knob, -1 to +1
Picks what a disrupted step does: SLICE plays a random other step, REVERSE SLICE plays one backwards, REVERSE PHASOR mirrors the position, SLOPE bends the ramp, STUTTER repeats it, FREEZE holds it
Scales the MODE CV before it is added to the knob, -1 to +1

inputs.text: The phasor to be cut up and randomised
Modulates the step count, scaled by the attenuverter and added to the knob
Modulates the chance, scaled by the attenuverter and added to the knob
Modulates the mode, scaled by the attenuverter and added to the knob
Above 1V every step is disrupted, whatever CHANCE is set to
Above 1V the randomisation runs; below that the phasor passes through untouched. With nothing patched here it runs

outputs.text: A 0-10V staircase, one level per step, following the step the output is playing
A 0-10V ramp across the current step while that step is being disrupted, and 0V the rest of the time
10V over the first half of each disrupted step, and 0V the rest of the time

notes: a phasor drives this, not a clock: a ramp rising from 0V to 10V once per cycle, from Phasor Generator, Clock to Phasor or an LFO's saw output. Nothing moves here until one is patched in.
